articles.description:
Composable Software in 2025: Building Systems Like Lego


Software in 2025 looks very different from what it did a decade ago. The shift from monolithic applications to modular, composable systems has become the new norm.  
Instead of giant, all-in-one apps, businesses are increasingly adopting the “Lego approach” — building digital products from smaller, independent pieces that can be assembled, swapped, or scaled as needed.  
Think of composable software as digital Lego bricks:  
Want a new payment system? Swap out a block.

Need advanced AI analytics? Plug in a new piece.

Looking for faster deployment cycles? Break things into smaller parts and iterate independently.



This flexibility allows businesses to stay agile in fast-changing markets while developers escape the headaches of ma…

articles.author: Uday Sai Savitha
articles.description:
[github] - https://github.com/udaybuilds47/resumebase
i graduated last december. it took me 6 months of grinding applications and endless rejections to land a role.
the market is brutal. the process is broken. and it’s not just about jobs, it’s about survival. our families, our careers, our self-worth are tied to this system.
so i started building. first applymate: a chrome extension to personalize resumes.
now resumebase: a job agent that reads the job, rewrites your resume, fills the forms, and applies for you.
right now it works, you drop a resume and a job link, and it applies. but it’s just the start. it still needs job search, recommendations, custom resumes, verification.
i’m building this alone. it’s slow. it’s hard. but it matters.
and i know it’s bigger than me.
so i’m open-sourcing everything i’ve built. design, engineering, product — whatever you can offer, let’s shape this together. let’s fix what’s broken.
agentics aren’t there yet — but they will be. and when they are, we should be ready. not crushed by the system, but owning our place in it.
whether you join me or not, i’ll keep building. but if you feel the same urgency, the same fire, then let’s build this together.
let’s get those jobs.
[github] - https://github.com/udaybuilds47/resumebase
articles.title: resumebase - an ai agent that applies to jobs for you

articles.author: Hiromis Rosa Martinez Marcet
articles.description:
When Code Consumes You: A Developer's Journey Through Obsession and Recovery | Hiromis Rosa Martínez Marcet
          
        
          
            When passion becomes obsession, sometimes the best code comes from stepping away from the keyboard.
After 2.5 weeks of 16-hour coding marathons building PersonaCode (my AI Code Assistant), I achieved everything I wanted: terminal integration, AI memory systems, adaptive UI, project management - a complete development environment.
Then everything broke. One feature update destroyed my memory system, and suddenly, my AI couldn't remember conversations from the day before.
For 3 days, I barely slept. Permanent headaches. Then I started bleeding from my nose - my body's way of saying "STOP."
My partner's ultimatum: "Rest or we fight." (First potential fight in almost a year - wasn't risking that!)
The breakthrough came in 4 hours of rest, not 72 hours of debugging.
Sometimes, the most productive thing we can do as developers is stop coding. The solution was a simple approach twist that gave me 90% of the results in half the time.
To my fellow developers drowning in code: Your vision will survive a few hours of sleep. Your health won't survive endless debugging sessions.
The screenshots show PersonaCode in action - floating panels, integrated terminal, adaptive theming, and real AI assistance. But the real lesson? Building sustainably is building smarter.
What's your experience with development obsession? How do you step back when code consumes your life?
#SoftwareDevelopment #AIAssistant #DeveloperLife #TechBurnout #PersonaCode #Sustainability
